what: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement via CDT
title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement via CDT
text: Constrained Delaunay triangulation refinement R, binding header-CDT library (MPL-2.0). takes input planar straight line graph (vertices, segments index pairs, optional per-vertex attributes) returns vertices, triangles, per-triangle depth says triangle sits relative constraints, point--polygon step.

title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement via CDT
text: Vertices segments , vertices triangles . square square hole: two closed rings segments. depth number constraint boundaries crossed way outside: 0 outside everything, nested rings odd inside, even hole. default triangles outside outermost boundary already dropped (erase = "outer", Triangle’s -p ); erase = "holes" also drops even depths.
code: library(cdtr) x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75) s0 <- 1:8; s1 <- c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5) r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1) str(r[c("P", "T", "S", "depth")]) #> List of 4 #>  $ P    : num [1:8, 1:2] 0 1 1 0 0.25 0.75 0.75 0.25 0 0 ... #>  $ T    : int [1:10, 1:3] 8 6 8 7 6 5 8 6 2 2 ... #>  $ S    : int [1:8, 1:2] 1 3 1 5 6 2 7 5 2 4 ... #>  $ depth: int [1:10] 2 1 1 1 2 1 1 1 1 1 plot_mesh <- function(m, main = "") {   e <- cdt_edges(m)   plot(m$P, asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = ".", main = main)   segments(m$P[e[, 1], 1], m$P[e[, 1], 2], m$P[e[, 2], 1], m$P[e[, 2], 2], col = "grey50")   segments(m$P[m$S[, 1], 1], m$P[m$S[, 1], 2], m$P[m$S[, 2], 1], m$P[m$S[, 2], 2], lwd = 2) } op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) plot_mesh(r, "constrained") plot_mesh(cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01), "max_area = 0.01") plot_mesh(cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25, erase = "holes"),           "+ min_angle = 25, holes erased") par(op)

title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement via CDT
text: Ruppert refinement always meet bound (two constraints meeting sharp angle, say). Rather silently stopping, result carries counts. min_edge_length floor refiner gives edge; default derived input (fraction median segment length, capped area target) refinement cascade sharp input corners. Pass 0 never-give-.
code: r2 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25) r2$unrefined #>   criterion shortEdgeTriangles circumcenterOutside circumcenterOnVertex #> 1      area                  0                   0                    0 #> 2     angle                  0                   0                    0 #>   sharpFixedCorner shortEdges splitVertexInvalid #> 1                0          0                  0 #> 2                0          0                  0 r2$min_edge_length #> [1] 0.025

title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement via CDT
text: polygon source reduces two tables. sf’s North Carolina counties, rings become vertex runs consecutive index pairs; shared boundaries dedupe one segment.  counties tile state, holes, county two boundaries coast depth 3, : depth peel layer, count constraint crossings outside, inside/outside flag general. computed topologically mesh alone, anything erased, makes cheap first cut classifying triangles region: nested rings get odd/even, coverage gets boundary-distance ordering, ties within layer need geometric lookup.
code: nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE) rings <- unlist(lapply(sf::st_geometry(nc), function(g) lapply(unclass(g), `[[`, 1)), recursive = FALSE) xy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rings, function(m) m[-nrow(m), ])) n <- vapply(rings, function(m) nrow(m) - 1L, 1L) start <- rep(cumsum(c(0L, n[-length(n)])), n) s0 <- seq_along(xy[, 1]) s1 <- start + (s0 - start) %% rep(n, n) + 1L m <- cdt_triangulate(xy[, 1], xy[, 2], s0, s1, max_area = 0.01) table(m$depth) #>  #>    1    3    5  #> 2100 1119  521 op <- par(mar = rep(0, 4)) plot_mesh(m) par(op)

title: Constrained Delaunay triangulation with refinement (CDT backend) — cdt_triangulate
text: x, y vertex coordinates s0, s1 1-based vertex indices constraint segment start/end (may NULL) max_area maximum triangle area (Ruppert refinement area), NULL none min_angle minimum triangle angle degrees, NULL none max_steiner budget Steiner points insert (Inf unlimited) min_edge_length refinement split edges triangles already shorter . NULL (default) chooses value input targets (see default_min_edge_length()): fraction median constraint segment length, capped never blocks max_area target. stops refiner cascading sharp input corners. Use 0 never give . min_edge_frac fraction median constraint segment length used min_edge_length NULL area_edge_frac fraction sqrt(max_area) caps default floor conforming TRUE use conforming (Steiner segments) instead constrained erase one "outer" (drop triangles outside segment-bounded region, RTriangle's -p ), "hull" (keep convex hull), "holes" (also drop even-depth regions). segments boundary, "hull" used. intersect crossing constraints handled: "resolve" inserts crossing point, "error" fails, "ignore" skips check angle_first criteria given, refine angle area (default area angle; two orderings differ little)

title: Constrained Delaunay triangulation with refinement (CDT backend) — cdt_triangulate
text: list P (vertices), T (1-based triangle indices), S (fixed edges), depth (per-triangle constraint layer depth: constraint crossings outside, 0 outside nested rings odd inside, even hole), n_input (vertices dedupe, Steiner), input_map (input vertex -> deduped vertex index), min_edge_length (value used), unrefined, data frame one row per refinement pass counting CDT refine (short edges, sharp fixed corners, )

title: Constrained Delaunay triangulation with refinement (CDT backend) — cdt_triangulate
code: ## a square with a square hole: two closed rings of segments x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75) s0 <- 1:8; s1 <- c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5)  ## constrained: every segment is an edge, depth says where each triangle is r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1) r$depth    ## 1 = inside the outer ring, 2 = inside the hole (nested rings) #>  [1] 2 1 1 1 2 1 1 1 1 1  ## refined, and the hole removed r2 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25, erase = "holes") nrow(r2$T); r2$unrefined #> [1] 96 #>   criterion shortEdgeTriangles circumcenterOutside circumcenterOnVertex #> 1      area                  0                   0                    0 #> 2     angle                  0                   0                    0 #>   sharpFixedCorner shortEdges splitVertexInvalid #> 1                0          0                  0 #> 2                0          0                  0  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = rep(0.5, 4)) for (m in list(r, r2)) {   e <- cdt_edges(m)   plot(m$P, asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = ".")   segments(m$P[e[, 1], 1], m$P[e[, 1], 2], m$P[e[, 2], 1], m$P[e[, 2], 2], col = "grey40")   segments(m$P[m$S[, 1], 1], m$P[m$S[, 1], 2], m$P[m$S[, 2], 1], m$P[m$S[, 2], 2], lwd = 2) }  par(op)

code: x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0); y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1) z <- 2 * x + 3 * y                 ## a linear field, reproduced exactly r <- cdt_triangulate_attr(x, y, 1:4, c(2, 3, 4, 1), PA = cbind(z = z), max_area = 0.02) range(r$PA[, "z"] - (2 * r$P[, 1] + 3 * r$P[, 2])) #> [1] 0 0
